title: AVIV Group: Building a European Real-Estate Platform from Acquisitions
basis: Reconstructed on 2026-11-12 from the published index.md (paragraph for paragraph, in its own order) and spec.md (accepted 2026-10-21), which it replaces. Intent outcome, the four journal acceptance criteria, the thesis and the role are copied unchanged from the case-aviv entry in journal-spec.json. A roadmap paragraph (p04) and a conclusion section (p55, p56; p56 is the published closing paragraph moved under its own heading) were added.

know: AVIV's four dated phases: assembling national portals (SeLoger 2010, Immoweb 2012, Immowelt and Immonet combined 2015, Logic-Immo 2018, Yad2, Meilleurs Agents 2019), moving up the seller funnel (Meilleurs Agents, the Ultimmo professional offer in November 2022, SeLoger opened to private sellers in 2023, commission-share seller leads), the 2021 integration intent, and the 2025 carve-out under KKR and CPP Investments with local autonomy and group functions.

Why real estate resists one platform (national feed formats, disclosures, address systems, agent software and pricing norms) and how thin AVIV's public record is: no engineering blog, talks or public code, so no AVIV system can be described.
believe: In real estate a group platform stops well short of the product, at the professional edge where the agent's software, the feed format, the disclosure rules and the pricing meet.
An integration goal needs a written layer-by-layer scope before it is staffed.
can_do: Draw the shared boundary of a multi-country property group by capability, saying what to share as platform, what as method, and what to keep local.

audience.who: Chief and enterprise architects of marketplace groups with property portals in several countries, and engineering leaders weighing a group platform after acquisitions.
already_knows: What an API, a database, an event stream, a search engine and Kubernetes are.
How to make and defend an architecture decision.
Part IX's evidence rules, from part-9, and the earlier cases' reading of shared layers.

Global components, tenancy and consolidation sequencing, from multi-country-platforms and platform-consolidation; real estate's national requirements, from vertical-requirements; multi-homing, from liquidity-and-network-effects.
does_not_know: AVIV's corporate history, owners and brands (SeLoger, Logic-Immo, Meilleurs Agents, Immoweb, Immowelt, Immonet, Yad2).
French real-estate terms: the agency mandate, DPE energy disclosures, DVF open transaction data, notary transaction records.
OpenImmo, the German real-estate feed standard.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Given a proposal for one platform across two countries' property portals, the reader uses AVIV's record to say which layers to share, which to keep local and what the decision record must state.
acceptance_criteria.probe: A property group running portals in two countries proposes a single platform for both, to be extended to future acquisitions. Using only this chapter: what does AVIV's dated record show about such a goal, which layers would you share, which keep local, and what must the decision record state?
acceptance_criteria.expected: AVIV's CEO announced in August 2021 the aim of 'aligning our tech roadmap across the organization to create a European real estate marketplace', with no published scope; by December 2025 the new Immowelt head described local autonomy with group-level functions 'where they create clear advantages'. Share infrastructure, data, identity tooling and engines, and valuation and ranking methods as group science; keep feed adapters, disclosure validation, professional products and lead routing local. The decision record states which layers are shared, which local, the markets in each stage, an exit criterion per stage, and the evidence that would change the split.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader of the opening alone (the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading) can predict the chapter's questions, its evidence and where it ends.
acceptance_criteria.probe: After reading only the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading: what questions will this chapter ask, what kind of evidence will it use, and how will it end?
acceptance_criteria.expected: One question (how much of a property portal can be shared across countries); evidence that is thin and corporate (corporate history, regulators' decisions, trade-press interviews, product announcements; no engineering material), enough to show the strategy's direction and the funnel it served but not to describe any system; the argument that national ingestion, disclosures, addresses, agent software and pricing make a group platform stop short of the product; a comparison applying that boundary to Veldmark's Hearthly.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reverse outline of the chapter, written without the spec, lists the same controlling ideas in the same order as the post spec's sections and paragraphs.

Every statement about AVIV's internal systems that no cited source documents sits in a callout or figure caption labeled as inference, and every company fact outside those labels carries its source and publication year.
acceptance_criteria.probe: Is there any sentence outside an `INFERENCE, NOT DOCUMENTED` callout or a labeled figure caption that describes how AVIV builds or runs a system without a dated source, or a company fact with no source and year?
acceptance_criteria.expected: None. Undocumented internals appear only in labeled inference callouts or captions; each company fact names its source and year in the sentence or the timeline; the author's interpretation is marked 'my reading' or sits in the Chief Architect's view.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The text attributes each statement of intent and outcome to its speaker: the 2021 goal is quoted as AVIV's CEO said it, and the phrase 'fully integrated platform' is shown to be the interviewer's, not AVIV's.
acceptance_criteria.probe: Does the chapter quote the 2021 CEO statement exactly ('...to create a European real estate marketplace'), avoid calling AVIV's goal 'unified', and make clear that 'fully integrated platform' comes from the interviewer's question in December 2025?
acceptance_criteria.expected: Yes: the 2021 line is quoted in full in the timeline and Phase 3; 'unified' is not used for AVIV's goal; the timeline, 'What was not said' and the reversal section each attribute 'fully integrated platform' to the interviewer.

thesis.question: How much of a property portal can a group share across countries, as AVIV's acquisitions, 2021 integration intent and 2025 turn to local autonomy show it from the outside?
thesis.claim: AVIV's documented integration moves were commercial and data-driven, not a shared listing platform: it shared valuation science and a bundled professional offer to capture sellers early and route them to paying agents, and its 2021 goal of 'a European real estate marketplace', never scoped in public, gave way by December 2025 to local autonomy with group functions 'where they create clear advantages'; the record therefore places a property group's shared boundary at infrastructure, data, engines and methods, short of the professional edge where national feed formats, disclosure rules, agent software and pricing norms meet, and it shows that an integration goal without a written scope cannot be changed cheaply.
thesis.disputed_by: The view that national property portals are similar enough (listings, search, agents, leads) for a group to run them on one European product platform, and that AVIV's 2025 reversal reflects its new owners' preferences rather than the vertical's limits.
thesis.so_what: A Chief Architect of a multi-country property group shares infrastructure, data, identity tooling and engines without hesitation, shares valuation and ranking methods as group science, and keeps feed adapters, disclosure validation, professional products and lead routing local; requires a layer-by-layer scope, markets per stage and an exit criterion per stage before staffing any integration goal; governs valuation as a supply product with an owner and published accuracy definitions; and builds the attribution chain behind commission-share revenue as local, consented and auditable work.
thesis.how_why: Axel Springer bought SeLoger (2010), 80% of Immoweb (2012), Immowelt combined with Immonet (2015, cleared by the Bundeskartellamt as Germany's second and third portals) and Logic-Immo (cleared in 2018), with Yad2 and Meilleurs Agents (bought for €200 million in September 2019 to 'widen the value chain'). Its integration moves were Ultimmo, one professional offer across SeLoger, Logic-Immo and Meilleurs Agents (November 2022), the 2023 opening of SeLoger to private sellers and seller leads monetized through commission share; Immowelt and Immonet still ran side by side nine years after combining. The 2021 CEO statement and the 2025 interview are the only public statements of intent and outcome; the phrase 'fully integrated platform' is the interviewer's. The carve-out became effective in April 2025 and a sale of Yad2 was signed in December 2025. AVIV publishes no engineering material, so the boundary is traced from strategy, not systems.

supporting_claims.claim: AVIV is a portfolio of national portals bought one at a time as whole businesses, and its public record is corporate, not technical, so every statement about its systems is either dated evidence or a labeled inference, and the open questions are listed rather than filled.

Real estate's national structure (agencies multi-homing through their own software, national feed formats, disclosures, address and property data, and pricing norms) puts the professional edge beyond the reach of a group platform.

AVIV's documented integration moves were commercial and data-driven: valuation science, a bundled professional offer within France and the opening of SeLoger to private sellers served one seller funnel, monetized locally through commission share, with no shared listing platform in the record.

The 2021 goal of 'a European real estate marketplace' was never scoped in public and gave way by December 2025 to local autonomy with group functions 'where they create clear advantages', a reversal whose size and cause the record does not show.

The record places a property group's shared boundary at infrastructure, data, engines and methods, short of the professional edge, and shows that an integration goal needs a written layer-by-layer scope before it is staffed.

role.contribution: Traces from the outside where a property group's shared boundary sits, and shows an integration goal of unpublished scope giving way to local autonomy.

additional_patterns.applies_to: resists to evidence-stops: cross-phase views (by national requirement, by asset type, by option, by risk, by gap)
chief-architect to questions: rules from the record, their test against the book and Veldmark, and questions for the reader's group

flow.rationale: Reading rules and the timeline come first because every later sentence is a dated fact, a reading or an inference, and AVIV's evidence is thinner than any other case's. The four phases run in time order because the case's lesson is a sequence: portals bought whole, a funnel shared commercially, an integration goal announced, then reversed; read out of order, the 2025 reversal would have no goal to reverse. The cross-phase views come only after all four phases because each one (the national requirements, the asset types, the trade-offs); the two readings of the record (by country, by asset type) come before the options they add up to uses facts from every phase; the evidence limits close that group so the rules that follow do not outrun them. The author's rules, the comparison and the questions come last because they apply what the record has shown (decision of 2026-10-19: four dated phases, because the evidence documents strategy direction, not systems). The phases overlap in time (the 2021 goal falls inside the 2019–2023 funnel phase): they are ordered by the start of each strand, so the funnel's products are read whole before the goal that ran beside them.

hook.content: Axel Springer bought national property portals one at a time (SeLoger in France, Immoweb in Belgium, Immowelt in Germany, Logic-Immo in France again) with an Israeli horizontal site, Yad2, and a French valuation business, Meilleurs Agents, gave them a common name and a common technology leadership, and in 2021 announced the goal of a European real-estate marketplace.

bridge.from_reader_world: A Chief Architect of a group that has bought property portals in several countries and is asked whether they should run on one platform.
bridge.to_topic: AVIV made that move in public, so its record can be read for how much of a property portal a group can share across countries, even though AVIV has published almost nothing about its systems.

thesis_statement.text: In real estate, ingestion formats, mandatory disclosures, address systems, agent software and monetization norms are national, so a group platform has to stop well short of the product; AVIV's documented moves (shared valuation science, a bundled professional offer, then local autonomy with group functions) trace that boundary from the outside.
thesis_statement.placement: KEY POINTS bullets 2 and 3 and paragraph p03.

promises.promise: Set the reading rules and the limits of the evidence, then give the dated timeline.
Follow AVIV's four phases in order: assembling national portals, moving up the seller funnel, the integration intent, and separation and local autonomy.
Look across the phases: why real estate resists one platform, the differences between asset types, the trade-offs, the failure modes and where the public evidence stops.
End with my decision rules, a comparison with the book's patterns and with Veldmark's Hearthly, and questions to ask of your own group.

sections.heading: Phase 1: Assembling National Portals (2010–2019)

advances_thesis.how: Shows the portfolio bought whole and the market structure that keeps the supply edge national.

flow.rationale: Three subsections: what was bought, what the regulators saw about those markets, and the two same-country pairs. The regulators come before the pairs because their description of multi-homing agencies explains why two portals in one country still face the same feed vendors. The correction of the German pair's merger date sits inside the pair's own paragraph, next to the 2015 combination, before the inference callout.

sections.heading: Phase 2: Moving Up the Seller Funnel (2019–2023)
sections.controlling_idea: AVIV's best-documented moves shared valuation science and a professional offer within France to capture future sellers and route them to paying agents, a funnel monetized locally through commission share.

advances_thesis.how: Documents the commercial and data-driven integration moves and shows them local by market.

flow.rationale: The French moves come in the order they were made (valuation bought in 2019, the professional offer in 2022, private sellers in 2023), each building on the one before; the revenue model closes the French funnel. Without the reading of valuation as a supply product (p22) before it, Ultimmo's seller detection would read as an arbitrary feature.

transition_in.introduces: The moves that did cross brands, from 2019.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Valuation is AVIV's best-documented business, because it was a product, not a platform.

evidence.what: Bought in September 2019 for €200 million; Axel Springer wanted to widen its French portals' value chain and share Meilleurs Agents' valuation expertise with its foreign sites.
evidence.shows: Shows the first sharing intent aimed at a method.

evidence.what: Figure 3: one method travels to three kitchens, each using its own local data.

sections.heading: Phase 3: The Integration Intent (2021–2024)
sections.controlling_idea: The integration phase is documented only as statements of intent, with leadership and hiring behind them and no published scope.

advances_thesis.how: Shows the 2021 goal and its unknown scope.

flow.rationale: What was said, then what was not said, then my reading of the gap; the reading needs both before it.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The integration phase began in 2021, while the French funnel was still being built, and is documented almost entirely by statements of intent: the 2021 CTO appointment and CEO goal, the 2023 hiring plan, the 2024 German rename and the 2024 signing release.

conclusion.heading: From AVIV to the Property Portals
conclusion.synthesis: Read in order, the four phases and the cross-phase views answer the chapter's question with one boundary seen twice: what AVIV shared in public (valuation science, a professional offer within one country, group functions 'where they create clear advantages') is what travels without touching the agent, and the 2021 goal and the 2025 shift are that boundary first announced without a written scope and then corrected in an interview.
conclusion.so_what: A Chief Architect who writes the boundary down layer by layer before staffing an integration goal can move it later without a write-off; one who does not inherits AVIV's position, a goal that could be reversed but never evaluated.
